Capability is compounding. The walls around AI agents are not coming down.

In the week of Sep 28, the Agent Restriction Index stood at 79 out of 100, from 5 restriction events across OS walls, platform bans, datacenter fights, safety exits and legal action. The index is holding without a statistically significant trend over 26 weeks (slope -1.1 points per month, Mann-Kendall p = 0.55). Meanwhile, since 2018 the largest AI training run has grown about 4.8× per year.

  • Safety exits OpenAI safety employee resigns, claiming the company’s ‘culture is broken’
  • Datacenter backlash Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash

What it means

Capability is on an exponential. The largest training run grows about 4.8× per year (doubling every 5 months), and the current record is GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) at 1.0×10²⁷ FLOP. 5 models above 10²⁵ FLOP shipped in the last 12 months, out of 23 ever. Agents built on these models now browse, click, buy and code on their own, and that puts them directly in front of every platform's walls.

The walls are real and frequent. 73 restriction events in 26 weeks: 1 os & app-store walls, 10 platform bans & blocks, 27 datacenter backlash, 4 safety exits, 31 legal & regulatory walls. The index is holding without a statistically significant trend over 26 weeks (slope -1.1 points per month, Mann-Kendall p = 0.55). As a check against news volume, the same score per 100 AI news items shows no significant trend (p = 0.57), so the index is not just tracking how much AI news gets written.

Capability is compounding while the walls hold at a steady height: 25 of 26 complete weeks had at least one restriction event (the quietest had 0). Steady walls against fast-compounding capability still produce more collisions each quarter, because the agents hitting the walls get more capable every month. Whether the walls themselves start climbing is what the next quarters of this index will show.

Method, sources and limitations

Score. Each week (Monday to Sunday, UTC), S = Σ category weight over deduplicated events dated that week. ARI = 100 × (1 − e−S/K), with K = 5.77 frozen on 2026-10-04 so that the median week of the calibration window scores 50. K stays fixed, so a reading of 70 today means the same thing as a 70 six months from now.

Classification. Headlines are matched against category rules that require the restriction itself to be in the headline (a wall verb plus an AI target: agents, bots, crawlers, AI apps or AI companies) along with AI context. Explainers, launches, deals and off-topic senses of "ban" are excluded. The same story reported by several outlets and on HN counts once.

Trend test. Mann-Kendall test on complete weeks, plus an OLS slope. A normalized series (score per 100 TechCrunch + Ars AI items) controls for swings in overall AI news volume.

Limitations. This is a measure of reported restrictions, so it inherits the news cycle's attention biases. Keyword classification is imperfect: expect a few false positives and misses each week (every counted event is listed above so you can audit it). OS-level restrictions often ship quietly in policy documents, so they are probably undercounted. Weights are judgment calls and are published here so you can disagree with them.

Corrections. Manual curation lives in data/ari_overrides.json (exclude an event id, add a missed event, or recategorize one), and it applies on the next rebuild.
